observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: an upright, pointed, teardrop-like body that curls to a hooked tip at the top. It is lavender/periwinkle with darker violet marbling. A pointed-oval amber window with swirling gold patterns sits in the middle of the body. Two long thin limbs splay out to the sides and end in flat pads. A short central stalk with a pad drops below the window. East: the same silhouette in profile, leaning right. The half-oval amber window is on the right (front) edge. The body is sea-green/teal with blue-lavender patches and rounded, cell-like bulges. It stands on a long rear limb, a forward limb and a short middle stalk. North: the same teardrop from behind, with no window or face. It is grey-green with mauve and faint gold marbling and stands on two splayed limbs and a central stalk. The three facings use visibly different colourings: violet on south, teal-green on east, greige/mauve on north.
observed.south.png: Full-resolution south view. Lavender/periwinkle teardrop with a hooked tip and a glowing amber oval window with gold swirls at its centre. Two thin splayed limbs end in pads, and a short central stalk sits under the window. Clean alpha, no outline, painterly soft shading.
observed.east.png: Full-resolution east view. Profile facing right. The body is teal-green with lavender-blue mottling and oval bubble-like cells, and is hooked at the top. A half-lens of amber-orange swirls on the right edge bulges forward. Thin rear and front limbs and a short middle stalk. Clean alpha. The hue is clearly greener than south.
observed.north.png: Full-resolution north view. The rear of the teardrop body is grey-green with soft mauve and faint yellow marbling and has no window and no eyes. Two splayed limbs and a central stalk. Clean alpha. The hue is greyer and more muted than south or east.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the candidate (east) stands in one cell beside the vanilla human. The creature is roughly half to two-thirds the human's height, consistent with about a metre. At 32 px/cell the creature reads as a small pale-teal spiky shape against brown ground, distinct from the rat and the human.
observed.siblings.png: Owner-kept adult blinker: a pale translucent blue/periwinkle teardrop with an amber oval window, the same three-limb stance and a thin dark-blue edge line. Its north view shows the amber window on the left flank. Anatomy, pose and canvas size match the candidate closely.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the front: the amber lens-window centred toward the camera, the limbs splayed symmetrically.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the plain rear of the teardrop with no lens-window, face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are upright elevation views at the game camera; none is top-down.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Heights measured at 190/181/185 px (5% spread); visually equal.

SIGNATURE.seen: The large amber lens-window with the yellow interior is the dominant feature on south and east and is legible.

ALIEN.seen: A hooked teardrop on crutch-like limbs with a glowing window has no Earth animal a stranger would name at first glance; the jellyfish likeness is only in the translucent texture.

DEPARTURES.seen: Departure 1, the soft upright teardrop body: present; the hue is a variant colouring, which the owner note allows. Departure 2, two thin trailing arms used like crutches with no legs: present on every facing. Departure 3, no face and a single lens-window with a yellow interior: present on south and east. Departure 4, a third shorter arm held over the lens: there is a short third limb, but it hangs below the window, as on the owner-kept sibling; it is not held over the window.

STYLE.seen: Soft painterly shading with marbled translucency and no heavy keyline; not cel-shaded, cute, photo or 3D.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art that matches the owner-kept blinker sibling; not vanilla or other-mod art.

ALPHA.seen: Every facing is cut out cleanly on the checkerboard with no ground patch, shadow or halo.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The variant matches the sibling in anatomy, pose, size and silhouette. The note asks for 'a distinct colouring', which implies one colouring, but the three facings carry three different colourings (violet, teal-green, grey-mauve), so the animal changes colour as it turns.

SCALE.seen: About half to two-thirds of the human's height in the scale panel, which fits 'about a metre tall'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell it reads as a pale spiky upright shape distinct from the brown ground.

reply.subject: RM_CanopySwinger__variant

observed.facings.png: Three facings on one shared scale. South is a compact, many-limbed creature seen from the front. Its small pointed head sits low at the centre, a striped tail curls up behind it, and six curling, hook-ended legs splay out at the sides. It is coloured in bright ochre/gold with dark brown bands. East is a long, narrow lizard-like body in profile. The head points right, the long tail curls into a spiral at the left end, and four tall, thin, multi-segmented legs end in curled hooks. It is coloured moss-green mottled with brown bands. North is a rounded rear view: a striped back, the tail spiralling down at the centre, and curled hooked legs at both sides. It is coloured brown with olive-yellow stripes. South and north look about the same size. East is much longer, as a profile of a long body would be.
observed.south.png: Front view. A small greenish-tan head with a pointed snout faces the camera at the lower centre, with a hint of eyes and a ridged crown. The banded tail curls up into a coil above the body. Six legs, three per side, bend outward and down and end in curled hooks. The legs are fairly thick and tentacle-like. They are banded gold and dark brown, more saturated and yellow than the other facings. The background is clean transparent alpha. There is a faint dark edge but no heavy keyline.
observed.east.png: Side profile looking right. The body is long and narrow, roughly 2–3 times as long as it is tall, plus a very long tail that ends in a tight spiral. The head is lizard/chameleon-like, with a ridged brow and a pointed snout. Four stilt legs each show an upper segment, a knee, a long shin and a further bend before a curled hooked foot, so the legs read as having an extra joint. The colouring is mottled moss green with diagonal brown bands, like vine bark. The background is clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view: a rounded, striped back and haunches, with the tail coiling down into a spiral at the centre bottom. No face or eyes are visible. Curling hooked legs stick out on both sides. The colouring is brown with olive/ochre stripes and a slight green cast. It is slightly shorter in height than south. The background is clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom, the candidate's east facing lies beside a vanilla human and spans a bit more than one cell long, low to the ground: a small slender animal. In normal play at 32 px per cell it reads as a thin dark squiggle with a curled tail and tick-like legs. It is thin but separable from the brown ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult ookala, in olive-brown woody bark tones with moss tufts. Its south has a small head, the tail curled above and six thin, angular, spidery legs with hooked feet. Its east is the long lizard-like body with four tall jointed legs and a spiral tail. Its north shows the back and a spiral tail with angular legs at the sides. The adult's limbs are thinner and more angular than the candidate's south and north limbs.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head and snout facing the camera at the lower centre, with the tail curled up behind it: a front view.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back and the tail spiralling down at the centre. There is no face and there are no eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: South and north are front and rear views at the game angle, matching the owner-kept sibling. East is a true profile. None is a rotated top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The code measured a 15% height spread, with north at 78 px against south and east at about 90 px. North is a compact rear pose with the tail coiled low, and the sibling's north is similarly compact. In facings.png south and north occupy similar boxes, so I read the spread as pose, not a size jump.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The anatomy matches across facings: hooked legs, spiral tail and narrow head. The palette does not. South is saturated gold/ochre with dark brown bands. East is moss-green mottled with brown. North is brown with olive-ochre stripes. In the side-by-side, south and east look like different colourways.

SIGNATURE.seen: The vine-like hanging climber reads: a long narrow body, a long prehensile spiral tail and hooked hands. The east bark-green mottling reads vine-like.

ALIEN.seen: The head and tail say chameleon, but the stilt-like, segmented, extra-jointed legs and the six-limbed front and rear views keep it from reading as a plain chameleon. It matches the owner-kept adult's design.

DEPARTURES.seen: (1) Elongated narrow body: present on east, the body is long and slim, well over twice as long as it is tall. (2) Extra joint per limb: present on east, each leg shows thigh, knee, long shin and a further bend before the foot. It is less legible on south and north, where the limbs curl like tentacles. (3) Hooked hands: present, curled hook feet on every facing.

STYLE.seen: Painterly texture with bark/vine banding. Not cel-shaded or a photo. South is slightly more saturated and graphic, but there is no heavy keyline and it is not cute.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art of this species, matching the sibling design. Not a vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: Clean transparent background on all three facings. No shadow, ground or backdrop.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Same species, anatomy, pose and canvas size as the adult, in a distinct colouring (greener and more banded than the adult's olive-brown). It reads as a colour variant. The silhouette differs only slightly: the south and north limbs are thicker and curlier than the adult's angular legs.

observed.facings.png: Three facings side by side, all at one scale. South: a squat, many-legged armoured scuttler seen head-on. The body is a central keeled head plate over a small fanged maw, with four or five clawed legs on each side splayed out and down. The plates are pale cream-grey with a dark crackle pattern; the legs are dark grey-brown fibrous cords between plate segments. East: the same body plan in profile, facing right. The back carries overlapping, spiny, ridged plates and a wedge-shaped head with a small dark eye and long curved fangs; six or more fibrous grey legs end in hooked claws. Here the plates are ochre/tan with dark brown mottling and fine crack lines, and the joints show pale grey corded gristle. North: a stacked pyramid of back plates ending in a point, with clawed legs fanning out to each side and no face. The plates are ochre/tan with dark mottling, like east. The south palette (cool grey-cream) visibly differs from the east and north palette (warm ochre).
observed.south.png: Front view of the scuttler at full resolution. A central diamond head plate with a ridge runs down to a fanged mouth cluster, and clawed legs splay symmetrically. The plates are cream-white to light grey with dark crazed cracks like dried mud. The legs and joints are dark grey-brown twisted fibrous cords. Clean alpha, no ground.
observed.east.png: Side profile looking right. The armoured back has saw-tooth plate ridges, and the elongated head has an eye and a jaw of long curved fangs. The legs are segmented, with grey corded gristle between the plates. The plates are ochre/golden-tan with darker brown blotches and fine crack texture. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view: the back plates stack into a pointed cone, with legs and claws fanning out on both sides. No eyes, no face. The plates are ochre/tan with dark brown mottling and a fine crack texture; the joints are grey fibrous gristle. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature stands beside the vanilla human as a small, low, spiky dark-grey shape about knee to shin height. At 32 px per cell it shows as a small grey speck beside the human and the rat, smaller than the rat's body length.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult gristleswarm (south, east, north). It has the same anatomy, pose and silhouette as the candidate: keeled head plate, fanged maw, spiny overlapping back plates, clawed fibrous legs. Its palette is a pale grey-green/beige plate colour with dark lichen-like blotches and pinkish-grey fleshy joints, consistent across all three facings.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head plate and fanged maw toward the camera, with the legs splayed symmetrically: a front view.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the stacked back plates rising to a point, with the legs fanning out; no eyes, maw or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are in the angled game camera with the legs reaching down to the ground; none is a plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Measured height spread is 3%. In facings.png the three bodies span similar widths and heights.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Same anatomy on every facing, but the palette differs: south plates are cool cream-grey with dark cracks and dark grey legs, while east and north plates are warm ochre/golden-tan with brown mottling. The animal changes colour as it turns.

SIGNATURE.seen: A scuttler of gristle and plate: armoured overlapping plates with corded grey gristle at every leg joint, plus a fanged maw for eating sinew and bone, legible in all views.

ALIEN.seen: Nearest is a crab or spider, but the many fibrous legs, wedge head with long fangs, saw-tooth dorsal plates and corded gristle joints make it read as an invented creature, not a recoloured crab.

OURS.seen: Clearly a recolour-level redraw of the kept RM_Gristleswarm sibling art, not vanilla or donor art.

ALPHA.seen: Checkerboard shows through everywhere around the body; there is no ground patch, shadow or halo.

East is a side profile: a long humped body with about seven transverse plates, the head and two curved antennae at the right end, and stubby conical legs below. observed.east.png: Side profile facing right. Long domed segmented shell, olive-green with cream, star-like blotches. A grey head with one eye and two thin curved antennae at the right. Several short pointed legs below. Clean alpha.

A knee-high, round-bodied creature called an ossivel, in its herd colour variant, shown as three views of one single animal in a row: a front view with the eyes toward the viewer, a side view, and a rear view seen from behind. Transparent background. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, with soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. The animal is knee-high to a person, a plump round body on short sturdy legs, carried low. It is far larger than a frog. The throat is formed as a row of organ pipes: eight to ten bone-cream tubes of graded length, tallest in the centre, set side by side across the front of the throat like a rank of organ pipes, each tube holding pale jade-green fluid.

ONE COLOUR VARIANT, IDENTICAL ON ALL THREE VIEWS. The body base is warm russet-copper. The soft rounded body lobes along the back and flanks are dusky plum with fine cream speckles. The pipe tubes are bone-cream. The fluid in the pipes is pale jade-green. The belly is a lighter sandy copper. These four colours sit in the same places on the front view, the side view and the rear view, so the three views read as the same animal turned around. The palette is warm copper, plum and jade, with no blue-white and no yellow anywhere on the animal.

Front view: the round body faces the viewer, the full row of bone-cream pipes with jade-green fluid is visible across the throat, the eyes are toward the viewer, and the plum lobes show at the shoulders. Side view: the animal in profile, the pipe row seen edge-on along the throat, the plum lobes with cream speckles along the back, the legs and body in russet-copper. Rear view: seen from behind, the rounded back and haunches in russet-copper with the plum lobes and cream speckles, the eyes hidden, and the tops of the jade-green pipes showing just past the shoulders.

Same body proportions, same number of pipes, same lobe layout and same four colours on every view. Natural, believable anatomy, lit softly from above.

observed.north.png: Full-resolution north: rear view. The back of a pointed head, chevron-patterned back plates, two haunches, and hooked limbs hanging down on each side. No face and no eyes. A darker brown overall with the same banding. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature stands beside the vanilla human, about half the human's height or a little less, low and spidery. At normal play (32 px/cell) it is a small thin grey-brown spidery mark on the brown sand ground, and its contrast with that ground is low.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult vekkit: the same three facings in pale grey/bone colour. The anatomy, pose, crest, hooks and silhouette match the candidate almost exactly. The candidate is the same body repainted brown with banding.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the front: the crested head faces the camera, and both hooked forelimbs reach toward the viewer symmetrically.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the head crest, chevron back plates and haunches, with no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are angled game-camera views. South and north show limbs hanging down to the ground and east is a profile; none is a top-down plan.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 11%, within 15%. The facings look comparable on the shared-scale panel.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The crest, the hooked forelimbs, the banded plates and the palette are present on every facing and turn with the body, matching the sibling layout.

SIGNATURE.seen: The two long jointed forelimbs ending in large hooks are the most prominent feature on all three facings, and the folding-chair angular legs are clear on east.

ALIEN.seen: It might suggest a mantis, but the knee-high size, the slatted crest head with no visible eyes, the plated folding body and the oversized hooks read as alien, not as an Earth insect.

DEPARTURES.seen: Departure 'knee-high body, far larger than an insect': present, about half human height in scale.png. Departure 'hinged, angular frame that folds like a folding chair': present, the angled legs on east read as a folding frame. Departure 'two long jointed forelimbs that end in hooks': present on all facings.

STYLE.seen: Painterly shading with no heavy keyline and no cute face. The banding reads slightly like polished carved wood, but the creature stays realistic.

OURS.seen: Own art that matches the owner-kept vekkit siblings; no vanilla or other-mod donor.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on all facings, with no ground patch, shadow or halo.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Same anatomy, pose, size and silhouette as the adult in siblings.png, painted in a distinct warm brown with dark banding instead of the adult's grey: it reads as the same species in a colour variant.

SCALE.seen: About knee- to waist-high beside the human at max zoom, which fits 'knee-high'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell on the brown ground in scale.png, the thin brown limbs give low contrast and the creature reads as a faint scribble rather than bold shapes.

findings.seen: At 32 px/cell the brown, thin-limbed body has low value contrast against the brown sand ground and reads as a faint scribble.

proposals: The brown banding has a smooth wood-grain look; a little chitin texture (matte plates, sharper segment edges) would keep the creature from reading as carved wood.

observed.facings.png: Three facings of a small, furry, six-legged creature at one scale on a checkerboard. South: an egg-shaped body seen from the front, pale grey with mauve mottling and a cream stripe down the centre. Two glossy black eyes and small mandibles sit at the bottom, with four jointed grey legs showing. East: a long, low profile. The body is dusky mauve-purple with darker blotches, and a ragged bone-white crest of fur runs along the back. The head is at the right, with one black eye and hooked fangs. Six segmented legs end in dark claw tips. North: a rounded rump in dark mauve with a white chevron pattern, and jointed legs splayed around it. No face shows. None of the facings has an outline. The silhouettes come from value contrast.
observed.south.png: The front view at full resolution. The body is a soft, painterly fur mass, mostly pale grey-lilac with darker mauve patches and a cream-white streak on top. At the base of the body are two dark glossy eyes and a pair of small fangs. Grey jointed forelegs hang down with darker tips, and smaller rear legs show at the sides. The alpha is clean.
observed.east.png: A side profile facing right. The underside and flank are a mauve-purple to plum colour with darker blotches. Shaggy bone-white fur forms a ridge along the top, with spiky tufts. The head has a single black eye and curved pale fangs. There are six slate-grey segmented legs in a walking pose, with darker claw tips. The style is painterly with no keyline. The alpha is clean, with no ground shadow.
observed.north.png: A rear view. The rump is a rounded fur mass in a dark mauve-plum colour with a white chevron or stripe pattern down the back. Six grey segmented legs with dark tips are splayed outward. There are no eyes and no face. The alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is a small grey-mauve bug, roughly the length of the human's hand, on the dirt tile. In the normal-play inset (32 px per cell) it is a tiny pale speck beside the human and the rat, visibly smaller than the rat.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult vennick: the same anatomy and pose on all three facings, painted pale grey with a bone-white back stripe and drawn with a heavy black outline. The south has two round eyes and fangs. The east is a long profile with a shaggy white crest. The north is a rump with a white stripe and splayed legs.

edits.change: One coat for every facing: the body flanks are pale grey, a soft cool light grey with light, low-contrast mottling. The back is bone-white. The south, east and north views share this identical pale grey and bone-white palette and the same mottling strength. Only the viewing angle changes between facings.

The bone-white back is one continuous band. It runs along the top of the body and reads as a light stripe that catches the gloom against the pale grey flanks. South shows it foreshortened down the centre line, east shows it along the top edge, north shows it running down the centre of the rear view.

Mottling is the same on all three facings: soft, light grey-on-grey blotches of equal contrast, with no darker plum or mauve patches. Value contrast between the grey flanks and the bone-white back carries the silhouette, with soft painted edges.

request.prompt: A single fist-sized silk-runner creature called a vennick, for RimWorld, drawn small and centred on a transparent background. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette, and the colour reads clearly at tiny size. Body: low, compact and quick, with slender legs built for running along thin high lines, and a head carried forward. Colouring, identical in every view: the body flanks, legs and underside are pale grey, a soft cool light grey with light, low-contrast grey-on-grey mottling, and the whole back is bone-white, one continuous bright band along the top of the body that catches the gloom against the pale grey flanks. The grey stays the same lightness and the mottling the same softness in every facing, so the south, east and north views read as one animal in one coat. The animal looks harmless and alert, a part of a swarm that moves like a current. Facings, drawn as three separate views of this same animal: south is the front view, eyes toward the viewer, the bone-white back visible as a bright band over the top of the body; east is the side view, head to the right, the bone-white back along the top edge and the pale grey flank below it; north is the rear view, seen from behind, showing the back, hindquarters and legs with the eyes hidden, the bone-white band running down the centre of the pale grey body. Style: flat even lighting from above, no cast shadow, no background scenery.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a squat, wide quadruped seen head-on, with a broad pale near-white belly, a wide grinning mouth lined with needle teeth, two short tubular eye stalks set high on the head, a central fringe of ivory spines rising from the crown, and four thick legs with large pale claws. East: a side profile of the same low, bloated body. Both eye stalks point to the right, the jaw is open with teeth, a row of spines runs along the back, a short pointed tail is at the left, and the belly is pale. North: the rear, with a broad back, a spine ridge running down the midline into a short pointed tail cone, haunches and splayed feet. Two rounded knobs at the top are the eye stalks seen from behind, and no face is visible. The hide is olive/grey-green with heavy dark-brown blotchy mottling. East looks a little greener and more saturated than south and north.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution. Wet, wrinkled, warty hide in grey-olive with dark brown blotches. Paler banded skin wraps the jowls. A near-white speckled throat and belly. A low-slung wide jaw full of needle teeth, with the lower teeth rising over the lip. The eyes are recessed openings at the tips of short ridged stalks. A spine crest climbs the forehead. The feet carry three to four thick ivory claws. Clean alpha with no ground patch.
observed.east.png: Side profile facing right. The body is long-ish but bloated and held low. Olive-green back with tan-yellow and dark mottling, and a paler cream underside. Two eye stalks project forward from the top of the head. The open jaw shows rows of teeth. Thin ivory spines run in a ridge from the head to the hips, and the tail is a short stub. Four stocky legs with clawed feet. Clean cut-out.
observed.north.png: Rear view. A grey-olive mottled back with a ridge of spines down the centre that ends in a short conical tail between rounded haunches. Hind feet splay out with claws visible from behind. The tops of the eye stalks show as rounded knobs over the shoulders. No eyes or mouth. Clean alpha.

East is a true side profile of a ceratopsian-like quadruped. The legs, belly and head are golden yellow-tan. A rust-red saddle runs along the back and is edged by a pale cream stripe. The frill and spikes run down the spine to a short tapering tail. North is the rear: haunches, a spiked spine and a tail hanging down. There is no face. Its pattern is a camouflage-like mottle of rust, dark brown and tan.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a front view of a stout fish. Two large ringed eyes face the camera, the lips are thick and downturned with a row of small teeth, there are blue-violet spines on the crown and two under the chin, and pale pectoral fins sit at the sides. A round ribbed tail fan stands up behind and above the head. East: a full side profile, head to the right. The body is olive-gold, with violet vertical bands and a scatter of violet dots behind the eye. The tail fan is pale with teal-green rays. There is a ridged dorsal crest with blue spines, a big ringed eye, a thick-lipped toothy mouth and blue chin spines. North: a rear view. The back is olive with violet and teal stripes and a ridged spine line, two blue spines stick up at the far (head) end, small pale pectorals show at the sides, and a ribbed tail fan in tan-yellow points toward the camera at the bottom. No eyes or face.

observed.east.png: Full-resolution east: a clean side profile. The olive-gold to pale-belly body has violet bands, and violet dots cluster on the cheek and upper flank behind the eye. The tail rays are teal/blue-green. The mouth is wide and thick-lipped, with visible teeth. Clean alpha, no shadow.
observed.north.png: Full-resolution north: a rear/dorsal view. Olive back with violet-teal stripes, spine ridge, two blue spines at the head end, and a yellow-tan ribbed tail fan toward the bottom. No face. Clean alpha.

request.prompt: A small gold-olive scalefish, the faa, a fast predatory fish of warm shallow water, painted as a game sprite in the painterly, realistic style of vanilla RimWorld, on a transparent background. Three views of the same fish: a front view with the eyes toward the viewer, a side view facing right, and a rear view seen from behind showing the back and the tail. Body: slim, streamlined and quick-looking, olive-green on the back shading into warm gold on the flanks and a paler gold belly, with fine overlapping scales. Head: slim and pointed, with a small mouth, a short neat snout tip, thin closed lips, an opening no wider than one eye and no visible teeth; the eye is bright and alert. Marking: one clear, straight row of 7 to 9 evenly spaced, round violet dots of equal size runs along each flank from just behind the gill cover to the tail base at mid-flank height. The side view shows the whole row. The front and rear views show the row along both body edges. Tail fan: the same colour scheme in every view, a warm gold-tan membrane with darker olive-brown rays, with only light and shade changing from view to view. Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. Bold, simple shapes that stay readable at very small size.

subject: RSW_Gutkurr__variant

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a hunched creature seen from the front. A big spiked dome shell covers it. Its armoured head hangs below the front of the shell, with red eyes, two long curved fangs and an open mouth full of teeth. Short dark maroon forearms end in black hooked talons. Thick yellow-tan thighs lead into dark segmented lower legs with big hooked claws. A segmented tail curls out to the viewer's left. East: a side profile facing right. The shell is a flared dome edged with spikes. The head is slung low and forward, with a red eye, a fang hooked down and gaping jaws. The thin forearms hang down with hooked claws. The insect-jointed hind legs are long and strong. A ridged tail curls behind. North: the rear. The spiked shell covers the top, and a row of cream spikes runs down the middle. Under the shell are two muscular tan thighs, dark lower legs and the forearm claws at the sides. A ridged, spiked tail tapers down to a hooked tip. There is no face. The shell is olive-khaki and brown with darker mottled camouflage patches. The thighs are yellow-tan, the lower limbs maroon-brown and the spikes cream.
observed.south.png: The front view at full resolution. The face looks toward the camera: red eyes, two long curved fangs, an open jaw with pale teeth. The domed shell is olive-brown and mottled, with cream spikes along its ridge and rim. The forearms are short and maroon, with hooked talons. The thighs are yellow-tan and the lower legs dark. The tail curls to the left. The cut-out is clean, with no ground or shadow.
observed.east.png: A true right-facing profile at full resolution. The flared shell has a camouflage pattern of olive, khaki and dark brown, with a row of cream thorns along its top. The head is low and forward, with a red eye, a downward fang and a toothy jaw. The hind legs are long, insect-jointed and powerful, the forearms thin and hooked. The tail is segmented and curls behind. The pose is a hunched stalking stance. The image is painterly, with fine texture. Its edges are dark but carry no heavy black keyline. The alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: The rear view at full resolution. The brown-olive shell dome narrows to a point at the top, with a centre row of cream spikes and spikes along the rim. Beneath it are muscular tan thighs, dark lower legs and claws. The forearm talons show at both sides. A segmented, spiked tail hangs down the middle to a hooked tip. No head, face or eyes show. The alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature spans about 3 cells, much larger than the vanilla human. At 32 px per cell it still reads as a dark spiky shell over a tangle of legs, clearly apart from the tan ground. Its olive-brown colour contrast with the ground is weaker than the adult's rust, but it is still legible.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult gutkurr in rust-orange, in south, east and north views. The anatomy, pose, proportions and spike layout match the candidate almost one for one. The candidate's tail, limb poses and shell shape follow the adult closely. Only the colouring differs.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face head-on: red eyes, fangs and an open jaw under the shell front.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the shell's back with its spike row, the thighs from behind and a hanging tail. There is no face and there are no eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three views are at the game's angled camera. North shows the shell's back slope with the legs beneath, not a top-down plan.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 15%. East is lower because the profile is a crouched stalk with the head forward, while south and north stack the shell over the legs. The kept adult sibling shows the same east-lower ratio. The width and body mass look equal, so the spread comes from the pose.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same shell pattern, spike rows, red-eyed armoured head, maroon forearm hooks, tan thighs and segmented tail appear on every facing. The tail turns correctly: it curls to the side on south, trails behind on east and hangs centred on north.

SIGNATURE.seen: The spiked, armoured dome shell, the powerful hind legs and the short hooked forearms are all large and legible.

ALIEN.seen: The creature is a bipedal-leaning shelled predator with a fanged, red-eyed head and a segmented tail. A stranger would not name it as a beetle or tortoise.

DEPARTURES.seen: Powerful hind legs: present, with thick tan thighs and long jointed lower legs. Short hooked forearms: present, thin maroon forearms with large black hooks. Spiked shell: present, with cream thorn rows along the ridge and rim.

CANON.seen: Body plan: hunched, long insect-jointed hind legs, short hooked forearms, domed shell, low forward head and segmented tapering tail, all present. Carapace: a flared skirt edge with cream thorn rows, present. Colour layout: this is the colour variant, and the owner note says to judge it as a variant. The lighter thighs, darker maroon lower limbs and cream spikes are kept; the shell is olive/khaki camouflage instead of rust. Head: wide armoured head with deep red eyes, two long curved fangs and pale teeth, present. Realistic, with no cartoon look. The NEGATIVE line is satisfied.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a tall quadruped viewed head-on. A narrow head with a red snout or bill is held low in front of a humped chest; a long tail sticks out to the left. Its pale cream-yellow hide carries dark brown vertical stripes, with grey-green mottling over the hump. Its legs are spindly with visible knees, and its feet are dark red-brown with split toes. East: a true side profile. The back rises to a high arched hump. A long neck hangs forward to a small head with a red face cap and bill, a blue-grey eye ring, small brow nubs and hanging neck flaps. A long tapering tail is held straight out behind and ends in a split fin-like tip. North: the rear, showing the hump, a green-mottled dorsal stripe running down into a tail that hangs down the centre, and the haunches and four legs. No face shows on north. All three facings have the same palette and anatomy.
observed.south.png: Full-resolution south facing: the front view with the red bill and red face cap at the centre, a blue-grey ring around each eye, and pale neck flaps under the head. A pale belly shows between the forelegs. Dark brown stripes run over the flanks and grey-green mottling covers the hump top. The tail projects to the left. The cut-out is clean, with no ground patch.
observed.east.png: Full-resolution east facing: a side profile walking to the right. The hump is high over the shoulders. The front legs are slightly shorter than the hind legs, and the long neck droops to a small head. The red bill, red cap, eye ring, brow nubs and dangling neck flaps are all visible. The tail is long and heavy, with a cream underside. The hide is painterly with skin-fold shading. No outline, and no shadow under the feet.
observed.north.png: Full-resolution north facing: the rear of the body. The hump is seen from behind, with a grey-green mottled stripe down the spine continuing into a tail that hangs down. Dark stripes run down the flanks, and the haunches and four legs show with red-brown feet. No head, face or eyes are visible. The alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature spans about 3 cells, and its hump top stands well above the vanilla human's head. In normal play (32 px/cell) it reads as a tall pale-yellow striped quadruped with a dark-feathered look against the brown ground, clearly bigger than the human and the rat.
observed.siblings.png: Owner-kept adult Jamel in south, east and north. The anatomy, pose and silhouette match the candidate closely. The sibling is a saturated golden-ochre with orange-brown stripes and blue-grey mottling. The candidate is paler cream-yellow with darker chocolate-brown stripes and greener mottling: the same species in a distinct colouring.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head-on face: red bill, both eye rings and neck flaps toward the camera, with the chest and forelegs in front.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the hump, the dorsal mottled stripe, the hanging tail and the haunches. No face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All facings use the angled game camera. None is a rotated top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 18%, but south's extra height comes from the front feet being placed lower and the body looming toward the camera. The owner-kept sibling shows the same south-taller pattern (sibling south about 324 px vs east about 276 px on its panel). The body width and hump size match across the facings, so the spread is pose and not a size jump.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The palette, stripes, hump, tail, red bill and feet agree on every facing. The tail turns with the body: to the side on south, straight behind on east, hanging centred on north.

SIGNATURE.seen: The high hump, spindly legs, long face and red bill are all clearly legible on south and east.

ALIEN.seen: The camel-like hump is offset by the reptilian long heavy tail with a fin tip, the red beak-like bill, the bare striped skin, the eye rings, the neck flaps and the clawed split-toe feet. A stranger would not call it a camel at a glance.

DEPARTURES.seen: Long face ending in a red bill: present (east and south). Yellow bare skin: present, a pale cream-yellow hairless hide with folds. Spindly legs: present, thin pillar legs with knobby knees.

CANON.seen: BODY PLAN: yes (tall, hump, shorter forelegs, neck hung forward, long tail straight out behind). COLOUR LAYOUT: yes, read as the variant: yellow hide, dark vertical stripes, blue-grey-green mottling on the hump, pale cream belly and tail underside, reddish-brown feet. Head: yes (narrow, red snout and cap, pale blue-grey eye ring, brow nubs, neck flaps). Feet: yes (splayed dark red-brown split toes with claws). Realistic rendering: yes. NEGATIVE: yes (no mane, no hooves, no harness or saddle).

STYLE.seen: Painterly, realistic hide with soft lighting and skin folds. No heavy keyline, not cel-shaded, not a photo or a 3D render. The eye is not cute.

OURS.seen: A bespoke painting matching the owner-kept sibling's anatomy. Not vanilla or donor art.

ALPHA.seen: Clean checkerboard around every facing. No ground patch, shadow or halo.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Same anatomy, pose, size and silhouette as the siblings panel, painted in a distinct paler cream with chocolate stripes and greener mottling. It reads as the same species, recoloured.

SCALE.seen: The hump stands well above the human's head at the same zoom, so it is taller than a person, as the canon says.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell it reads as a pale striped quadruped with a hump and a long tail, distinct from the brown ground. The pale tone is a little lower in contrast on sand-coloured ground than the sibling's ochre, but it still reads.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a pale grey six-legged arachnid-like creature seen from the front. A tall upright egg-shaped abdomen rises above a small low head with black bead eyes and two short curved hooked mouthparts. The abdomen is pale grey with broad rust-pink marbled bands and fine dark crack lines. East: the same body plan in side profile, with the abdomen tilted up and back. This abdomen is grey and heavily mottled with mossy olive-green patches, with only a faint pink wash on its lower front. The head looks right with two visible eyes and hooked palps. North: the rear view. The oval abdomen is grey with rust-pink diagonal bands like the south view, and the small head behind it shows only two palp hooks and no eyes. All six legs are long, bony and many-jointed, with knobby greenish-grey joints and dark curved claws. The heights look similar across the facings.
observed.south.png: The front view alone: a grey egg abdomen with pink-rust marbling and crack lines, a small flat face low between the legs with about three or four black bead eyes, two curved dark pedipalp hooks, and six sprawling bony legs with dark claws. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: The side profile alone. The abdomen is grey and covered in green lichen-like blotches, with a slightly pinkish underside. The head on the right has two black eyes and hooked palps. Several bony legs with knobby joints and dark claws. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: The rear view alone: an oval abdomen with diagonal pink-rust bands and crack lines, a small head peeking out above it with two palp hooks and no eyes, and six legs sprawling outward. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At 128 px per cell, the east facing beside a vanilla human. The creature is roughly 2.5 cells wide and about 2 cells tall, well over a human's height. At 32 px per cell it reads as a pale spidery shape with a tall abdomen next to the human and the rat.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept base krykna: south, east and north. The body plan, pose and silhouette are the same as the candidate. The whole body is ivory/pinkish-beige with fine crack lines and no banding or green mottling. The base colouring is the same on every facing.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face toward the camera: black bead eyes and hooked palps low between the front legs, with the abdomen rising behind.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the rear of the abdomen. Only the back of the small head and the palp tips show above it. No eyes and no face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: No facing is a rotated top-down view. North is a high rear view that matches the owner-kept sibling north.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 7%, and the facings panel confirms visually similar sizes.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Anatomy matches on every facing, but the palette does not. South and north abdomens are grey with rust-pink marbled bands. The east abdomen is grey with heavy olive-green moss blotches and almost no pink banding. Turning in game would swap the variant's colouring.

SIGNATURE.seen: The towering egg-shaped abdomen, six legs and low beaked face are all clearly legible.

ALIEN.seen: A spider is the nearest animal, but the six bony knobbed legs, the tall upright egg abdomen and the tiny low face make it read as an alien creature, not an Earth spider.

DEPARTURES.seen: Six legs: yes, three per side counted on north and south. Abdomen rising tall: yes, upright on south and tilted up on east. Low beaked mouth: yes, short curved hooks under a small face, no large fangs or mandibles.

CANON.seen: Body plan: yes. Pale bone-grey skin with crack lines and green-grey joints: yes. Dark claws: yes. Black bead eyes: yes, though south shows about 3–4 and east 2. Beaked mouth with curved palps: yes. Realistic, no outlines: yes. Not eight-legged, hairy or black chitin: yes.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, realistic shading with pitted hide texture and no keylines. It matches the sibling's rendering.

OURS.seen: It is a recolour-style variant of the owner-kept krykna with its own painted pattern, not a vanilla or other-mod donor.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on every facing: no ground, shadow or backdrop.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Same anatomy, pose, size and silhouette as the sibling, in a colouring distinct from the adult. But the note asks for one distinct colouring, and the east facing carries a different colouring (green moss) from south and north (rust-pink bands). So the variant does not read as one consistent look.

SCALE.seen: About 2 cells tall beside a 1-cell human, which fits 'clearly larger than a human (2 m tall)'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a pale tall abdomen over a spray of thin legs, apart from the brown ground.

findings.seen: The east abdomen is grey with heavy olive-green lichen mottling and only a faint pink underside. The south and north abdomens are grey with broad rust-pink marbled bands and no green mottling.
findings.quote: facings disagree on anatomy/palette, or a structure does not turn with the body
findings.fix: Paint the east abdomen with the same grey base and broad rust-pink marbled bands as the south and north facings, in the same proportions and with no green mottling (or repaint south and north to match the east's green mottling, so all three facings carry one colouring).

findings.seen: The variant is meant to be one distinct colouring of the krykna. Instead the east and the south/north facings carry two different colourings.
findings.quote: It must read as the same species as the adult in the siblings panel: same anatomy, pose, size and silhouette on the canvas, painted in a distinct colouring.
findings.fix: Give all facings one shared variant colouring, a single pattern that reads the same from front, side and rear.

request.prompt:
A krykna, a pale six-legged predator from Atollon, painted as one distinct colour variant, for a top-down RimWorld creature sprite on a transparent background. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette.

Body plan: six legs, not a spider's eight, jointed and sturdy, carrying the body low to the ground. The abdomen rises tall above the body like a towering dome or column, not slung low behind it. The head is small and low-set, with a short beaked mouth in dark horn-grey, with no fangs or mandibles. The pose, size and silhouette match the owner-kept sibling krykna.

Face, in the front view with the eyes toward the viewer: four round, glossy black bead eyes in two clear pairs, set above the beaked mouth, with a visible gap between the pairs.

One variant colouring on every view (front, side and rear). The hide is pale grey. The tall abdomen is the same pale grey base with broad, soft rust-pink marbled bands wrapping around it, with a faint pink flush on the underside. The rust-pink bands keep the same proportions and the same positions on the abdomen from the front view, the side view and the rear view. The abdomen is smooth grey and rust-pink only, and the legs and body share the same grey with the same faint pink at the joints. The side view shows the same bands as the front and rear views, seen as the body turns.

Views: front view shows the face and the beaked mouth, with the abdomen rising behind and above the head. Side view shows the six legs in profile and the full height of the abdomen. Rear view, seen from behind, shows the abdomen and the back of the body, with the eyes hidden.

The animal is alive, alert and predatory. Transparent background.

subject: RSW_Lylek__variant

reply.subject: RSW_Lylek

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a spidery insectoid. A small spiked wedge head with red eyes sits above a round, gaping, toothed maw. Two spiked pincer-arms are raised on either side, and each pincer-tip looks like a small head with a red eye. The thorax plates are spiked and leaf-like. A pale cream scaly underbelly hangs between about eight long, stiff, spike-tipped stilt legs splayed outward. Two long dark tentacles with pale undersides loop down and outward from the front of the torso. East: the same creature in side profile, head and maw toward screen right, pincers raised in front and behind the head, legs angled out like stakes, and both tentacles trailing and coiling below. North: the rear of the same body. The back of the head is a spiked plate crest with no face or eyes. The backs of the pincers are raised, the legs splay out and the tentacles hang down. Colouring on all three: tan/ochre carapace with heavy dark brown-black tiger-like bands, cream joints and underbelly, dark tentacles with pale undersides. North is a little darker and greener-brown.
observed.south.png: Front view at full size. The face and round maw point at the camera, the red-eyed pincer-heads are raised symmetrically, the striped spiked carapace is sharp and painterly, and the cream underbelly and both tentacles curl out to the sides. Clean transparent background, no outline keyline.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. The wedge head has an open toothed jaw and the round maw shows below it. The pincers are raised fore and aft. The torso is slung between stiff spear legs. One tentacle sweeps far left and the other coils under the belly. Striped tan and brown plates. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view. A tall spiked dorsal crest runs up to the back of the head. No face, no eyes, no maw. The pincer-arms are seen from behind. The legs splay out in a symmetric tripod-stake fan, and the tentacles hang from under the torso with one curled. The colouring here is darker olive-brown with fainter bands. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature fills about 4 cells and towers over the vanilla human, roughly 3 times the human's height. At normal play (32 px/cell) it reads as a large spiky, leggy shape with raised arms, clearly apart from the tan ground, and far larger than the human and the rat.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult: the same anatomy, pose, silhouette and tentacle placement on all three facings, painted moss/olive green with cream underbelly. The candidate matches it nearly line for line in shape. Only the palette differs: tan with dark brown banding instead of green.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face, red eyes and the round toothed maw toward the camera, with the pincers raised symmetrically.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the dorsal spiked crest and the backs of the pincers. No eyes, maw or face are visible.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are side/elevated game-camera views of a standing creature. None is a top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Measured spread is 14%, within 15%. The facings look comparable on the shared-scale panel, and north is tallest because the crest shows from behind.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Head, both pincers, the stilt legs, both tentacles and the cream underbelly appear on every facing and turn with the body. The palette is consistent, with north slightly darker in shading.

SIGNATURE.seen: The spear-like legs, raised spiked pincers, two long tentacles and the toothed maw are all plainly legible.

ALIEN.seen: The nearest animal is a spider, but the raised head-like pincers, the round toothed maw, the long whip tentacles and the upright neck make it clearly not one. A stranger would not call it a spider with parts bolted on.

DEPARTURES.seen: Departure 'stands tall on long, spear-like legs': present, stiff spike-tipped stilts. Departure 'raised pincers covered in spikes, not mantis grasping forelegs': present, spiked pincer-heads held up. Departure 'two long tentacles around the mouth, beside powerful mandibles': present, two long tentacles from the front torso plus a toothed maw and jaws. Departure 'ridged carapace': present, jagged ridged leaf-like plates.

CANON.seen: The body plan, the head and head-like pincers with red eyes, and the long dark tentacles with pale undersides are all present. The rendering is realistic with no outline, and the body is not a beetle or plain spider. The canon colour line (olive/moss green) is replaced by tan with dark banding, as the owner note on the colour variant directs. The layout of the colours (darker recesses, pale underbelly and joints, dark-over-pale tentacles, red eyes) is kept.

STYLE.seen: Painterly chitin texture with natural lighting and no heavy keyline. Not cute or cel-shaded, not a photo or a 3D render.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art matching the owner-kept sibling's anatomy. No vanilla or other-mod donor.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on the checkerboard and on white. No ground patch, shadow or halo.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Same anatomy, pose, size and silhouette as the sibling adult on all facings, in a clearly distinct tan with dark tiger-band colouring.

SCALE.seen: Towers about 3 times the human's height, fitting a 'large insectoid predator' standing high on stilts.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell it reads as a big spiky leggy form with raised arms and dark tentacle loops against the ground. The thin legs stay visible as spikes.

proposals: For colour-variant subjects, let the card mark the canon COLOUR LAYOUT line as hue-exempt (the layout of light and dark still applies), so a reviewer does not have to reconcile the canon hue with the variant owner note each time.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one shared scale on a checkerboard. South is a heavy striped quadruped seen head-on: two tall, pale, branching antlers rise from the back of the skull, and a long down-turned snout with a pale thick-lipped muzzle hangs low. A tufted striped tail curls out to the viewer's left. East is a true right-facing profile: a barrel body with a shoulder hump higher than the rump, a sagging pale belly, four short thick dark legs, the head carried low near the ground, and antlers that are the tallest point. North shows the rump and the tufted tail, with the antlers behind the back and no face. The coat is a warm tan or ochre ground with broad dark-brown vertical stripes, and the shoulders and neck are a solid darker brown. The three facings are close in height.
observed.south.png: Front view with the face toward the camera. Low head, a long flexible snout that ends in a pale, rolled, thick lower lip, small eyes, and a few pale dot markings on the brow. Two cream antlers with several tines rise straight up. Broad padded feet with pale toes and claws. Stripes run over the flanks, and the tail tuft shows at the left. The ground colour has a slightly olive or khaki cast. Painterly fur with a thin dark edge, and no heavy keyline.
observed.east.png: Side profile facing right. Squat, heavy, long body with a hump over the shoulders. Bold dark-brown vertical stripes run over the back, flanks, rump and upper hind legs on a warm orange-tan ground. The neck and shoulders are dark brown, the belly is cream, and the lower legs are the darkest part. A pale curved claw shows on the front foot. The snout is long and down-turned with a pale muzzle and wrinkled skin. The striped tail hangs and ends in a dark tuft near the ground. The antlers are branching and somewhat palmate, and they rise straight up from the back of the skull. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view: rump, haunches and a striped tail with a tuft hanging to the ground. No face and no eyes. The antler tips rise behind the back and the shoulders, which carry a reddish-dark-brown patch. The hind legs are dark below with padded feet. The ground colour here is a little paler and creamier than in east. Clean alpha. The body sits right of centre on its canvas.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the animal is about 2 cells long and roughly as tall as the human at the antler tips. Its body is bulkier than a human, which reads as a squat heavy herbivore. At 32 px per cell it still reads as a striped barrel body with pale antlers apart from the brown ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult runyip (south, east, north): the same anatomy, pose, antler shape, snout and tail, with a whitish-cream ground and narrower, denser black-brown stripes. The same hide hue, band colour and mantle tone appear in every view.

The grey-green body colour is stated as a body-wide property: in the east (side) view and the north (rear) view the hide is the same sage grey-green as the front view, with the same pale blue-grey banding on the mantle. No brown, umber, tan or khaki in the hide.

The variant reads as one distinct look: a lighter, cooler sage grey-green with pale blue-grey bands, clearly lighter and greener than the adult's dark slate. This single colouring is applied identically on every facing.

invariants: Anatomy, pose and silhouette match the adult sibling's: heavy quadruped body, huge ridged mantle over the neck and back, two tusks
Sage grey-green hide with pale blue-grey bands, identical on south, east and north
Thick, heavy hide texture and ridged mantle shape
Transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, soft painted edges; value and colour contrast carry the silhouette
Size and proportions for a 3.8 x 3.8 draw size creature
request.prompt: Three views of one skalder, a heavy herbivore from Florrum, in its variant colouring: front view with eyes toward the viewer, side view, and rear view seen from behind with eyes hidden. All three views show the same animal in one shared colour scheme. The hide is a muted sage grey-green of medium value, with pale blue-grey bands across the mantle ridges and along the flanks. The tusks are pale bone-cream. The grey-green hide covers the whole body in every view: in the side view and in the rear view the hide is the same sage grey-green as in the front view, with the same pale blue-grey banding and the same mantle tone. The variant looks lighter, cooler and greener than the adult's dark slate. Body plan: a heavy, thick-hided, broad quadruped with a huge ridged mantle covering the neck and back, rising in layered ridges that show clearly from the front, the side and from behind, and two tusks curving from the lower jaw. The thick hide has a rough, weathered, leathery texture. The pose, proportions and silhouette follow the adult sibling's render, as the reference image shows. Transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic rendering with soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette.

subject: RSW_Snoruuk__variant

observed.facings.png: Three mushrooms on a checkerboard, all the same size: a broad domed cap in deep crimson or maroon, a lilac-grey gill fringe under the cap rim, and a thick, slightly wavy, pale cream stalk. The stalk splits at the base into two rounded lobes. The cap carries irregular blotches: tan and ochre on all three facings, dark maroon on south and north. The stalk carries round spots in dark brown (south, north) or olive-brown (east). The east facing's stalk leans and its cap tilts slightly, which gives a side view. The rendering is painterly and matte, with fine fibrous texture and no outlines. There is no face, eye or limb.
observed.south.png: A front view of the crimson-capped mushroom. The cap is symmetric with a scalloped rim, and the grey-lilac gills show under the rim. The pale stalk carries round dark-brown spots and ends in a two-lobed flared foot with dark-tipped lobes. The background is clean and transparent, with no shadow.
observed.east.png: The same mushroom from the side. The cap is tilted slightly, so more of the gill underside shows on the left. The stalk bends gently, and its spots are olive and brown. The two-lobed foot is still visible. The alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: The same mushroom from the opposite side. The cap blotch layout differs: large dark maroon patches and a few tan ones. The stalk spots are larger and dark brown, and the foot lobes are dark-tipped. There is no face. The alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom, the mushroom fills about two thirds of one cell beside a vanilla human, smaller than the human. At 32 px per cell, a small red cap on a pale stalk reads clearly against the sand ground, about the size of the rat.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult snoruuk: the same anatomy, size, cap shape, gill fringe and two-lobed spotted stalk, painted with a bright orange cap with darker red-brown and pink blotches and a tan stalk with brown spots.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South is the symmetric front elevation of the mushroom. The subject has no face by design, and south carries the same cap and stalk as the sibling's south.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the opposite side of the cap and stalk, with a different blotch layout and no face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are side or three-quarter elevations with the gill underside visible. None looks down onto the cap.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Code measured a 2% height spread, and the facings panel shows equal size.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Every facing has the same crimson cap, grey gill fringe, pale spotted stalk and two-lobed foot. Only the spot placement changes, which is natural for a turned body.

SIGNATURE.seen: A red mushroom, with a clearly legible red domed cap on a stalk.

ALIEN.seen: This is a canon subject, and the description names its Earth body (a mushroom), so the alien test does not apply.

CANON.seen: Present: the domed cap, the scalloped gill-fringed rim, the thick stalk with a flared foot, the red colour, spots on cap and stalk, matte realistic rendering without ink outlines, and no face, eyes or mouth. The group-of-several line is an Engine limit for a single pawn sprite. Two points are minor: the cap spots are irregular blotches rather than round blisters, and the split foot hints at legs. The kept sibling shares both points, so neither is a miss.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, matte, with fibrous texture and soft lighting. It has no keyline, no cel shading and no cute features.

OURS.seen: Own art that matches the kept sibling's hand. It is not a vanilla or other-mod donor.

ALPHA.seen: Every facing has a clean transparent background with no ground patch or shadow under the foot.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The variant has the same anatomy, pose, size and silhouette as the sibling adult and a distinct colouring: deep crimson cap with tan blotches and pale cream stalk, against the sibling's orange cap and tan stalk.

SCALE.seen: At about two thirds of a cell, the mushroom is smaller than the human, which fits a small mobile mushroom with drawSize 1.0.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell, the red cap and the pale stalk read as two bold shapes apart from the sand ground.

reply.subject: RSW_Tibidee__variant

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. Every facing shows the same plan: a plump flier with two very long pointed V-shaped wings, a segmented tail, a broad flat head, and grey-blue claws under the belly. South is the front: a warm tan/beige body and wing tops with fine dark-brown leopard-like mottling, a deep red wing membrane, and two yellow eyes on a broad flat face. East is a side profile facing right: the wing top is cool grey with large olive/charcoal camouflage blotches, the belly is pale grey-white, the membrane is crimson-maroon, and there is a dorsal fin, a long segmented tail, a yellow eye and a wide mouth line. North is the rear: a grey-green back with a dark central ridge, wing tops in charcoal with cream/white flecks, a rust-orange wing underside, a tail hanging down, and no face. The three facings differ visibly in base colour and pattern: warm tan, then cool grey-olive camouflage, then charcoal with white flecks.
observed.south.png: Front view, face to the camera: two yellow eyes on the sides of a broad flat head, a heart-shaped muzzle, two blue-grey claws tucked below, the segmented tail curling up behind the head, and both wings raised in a V. The body is warm sandy beige with fine dark mottling on the wing tops. The membrane is a deep red. Clean alpha, no outline.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. A long swept wing rises up and back. The wing top is grey with big dark olive camouflage patches, and the membrane below is red-maroon. A pale grey plump belly, a small dorsal fin, a long segmented tapering tail, a yellow eye on the side of a flat head, a wide mouth line, and blue-grey claws under the belly. Painterly, no outline, clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view: a V of wings with charcoal tops broken by cream/white flecks and an orange-rust underside. A central spinal ridge runs over a grey-green back, small side fins sit at the hips, and a segmented tail hangs down. No eyes or face. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: The east facing beside a vanilla human and a rat at 46 px/cell and at 32 px/cell. The creature spans about 7–8 cells and dwarfs the human, which fits 'giant'. At 32 px it reads as a big pale-bellied flier with a long dark wing and a red underside. The camouflage blotches are still visible.
observed.siblings.png: Owner-kept adult: the same anatomy, pose and silhouette on every facing. It is consistently pale cream-white with fine speckling, pale wing-edge stripes and a red membrane, and the colour scheme matches across south, east and north.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face head-on: two yellow eyes, a broad flat head, a muzzle and the claws below.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back ridge, the hip fins and the hanging tail. No eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: The facings are front, profile and rear at the game camera, matching the sibling poses. None is a rotated top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 4%, and the facings are visually equal in facings.png.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The anatomy matches and the structures turn with the body, but the palette does not. South is warm tan with fine brown mottling and a deep-red membrane. East is cool grey with large olive camouflage blotches and a crimson membrane. North is charcoal with cream/white flecks and a rust-orange membrane. The variant's colouring changes as the animal turns.

SIGNATURE.seen: The giant long pointed membranous wings, the plump torso, the broad flat head and the long segmented tail are clear on every facing.

ALIEN.seen: A gasbag body with huge V-wings, a fish-like flat head and a segmented tail. It does not read as a bat, bird or any Earth animal.

CANON.seen: Drawn in flight with long tapering wings, a plump torso, a broad flat head and a segmented tail. The wing tops are mottled and the membrane is red/red-brown. Blue-grey claws sit under the belly. Yellow eyes are on the sides of the head, and east shows a wide mouth. The rendering is realistic with no outlines. It is not bat-dark or feathered. The body colour departs from pale white-grey, which the owner note allows for the colour variant.

STYLE.seen: Painterly shading, natural membrane veining, no keyline and no cute face.

OURS.seen: Own art matching the owner-kept tibidee anatomy, not a vanilla or donor animal.

ALPHA.seen: A clean cut-out on every facing, with no shadow, ground or halo.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The same anatomy, pose, size and silhouette as the siblings are honoured, and the colouring is distinct from the adult. But the note asks for 'a distinct colouring' of one variant look, and the three facings carry three different colourings (tan mottle, grey-olive camo, charcoal with white flecks), so the look is not one consistent variant.

SCALE.seen: Spans about 7–8 cells beside a human at drawSize 8, which fits 'giant'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell the dark wing, red underside and pale belly read as bold shapes against the brown ground.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. All three show the same anatomy: a segmented crustacean body with a pair of curled, claw-like pincers arching over the rear, two long whip antennae and short jointed legs. The colouring is different on every facing. South is a saturated golden yellow-olive with dark brown mottling. East is a pale sage green and off-white camouflage mottle with thin golden rims on the plates. North is a dull olive-khaki with bold reddish-brown bands across the pincers and back plates.
observed.south.png: A front view. Mouthparts, feeler-like palps and the forward legs face the camera at the bottom centre, and two long antennae sweep out to the sides. The tail pincers curl up behind the body at the top. A tapered head plate points down toward the viewer. The colouring is golden yellow-olive with dark brown blotches. The cut-out is clean with no ground under the body.
observed.east.png: A true side profile facing right. A small dark eye and a spray of antennae and palps are at the right, a long body of overlapping armoured segments runs along the middle, and walking legs sit underneath. The two curled pincers rise from the tail end at the left. The colouring is a pale sage and cream camouflage mottle with gold-edged plate rims. The alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: The rear view. Banded back segments end in a fanned tail plate at the bottom, and the legs splay to the sides. The two pincers curl up at the top and the antennae extend sideways. There are no eyes or face. The colouring is olive-khaki with strong reddish-brown banding, which differs from both the south and east facings. The alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the east facing is shown on sand beside the vanilla human. The animal is about half a cell long and well under the human's height. In the normal-play inset at 32 px per cell it is a tiny pale, sage-coloured fleck next to the rat.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult Yobshrimp is in a uniform pale bone/cream colouring that matches across south, east and north. It has the same anatomy, pose and silhouette as the candidate: tail pincers arching over the back, long antennae, and an armoured segmented body.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the mouthparts, palps and forward legs toward the camera, with the head plate pointing at the viewer. The tail pincers are behind the body.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the banded back and the fanned tail plate at the bottom, with no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings use the angled game camera and match the owner-kept adult's views. None is a rotated top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 8%, and the facings look matched in the facings panel.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The anatomy matches and turns correctly, but the palette changes on each facing: golden yellow-olive on south, pale sage and cream camo on east, olive with red-brown bands on north. In game the animal would change colour as it turns.

SIGNATURE.seen: The yobshrimp body plan is legible on all facings: the armoured segmented body, the curled tail pincers and the long antennae. The east facing reads as pale, as the description says.

ALIEN.seen: The description names its Earth body (a shrimp), and the art matches the owner-kept adult's invented anatomy with tail pincers.

STYLE.seen: The art is painterly and realistic, with shaded chitin plates. It has no keylines and nothing cute, cel-shaded or 3D-rendered.

OURS.seen: This is new painted art for the variant, not a vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: All facings are clean cut-outs on transparency, with no shadow, water or ground.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Each facing keeps the adult's anatomy, pose, silhouette and size and uses a colouring distinct from the adult's bone-cream. The cross-facing palette mismatch is reported under SAME_ANIMAL.

SCALE.seen: At drawSize 0.8 it is a small juvenile, about half a cell long and far smaller than the human, which fits 'too small yet to swarm'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a small pale elongated shape against the sand, though it is tiny.

findings.seen: The colour variant uses three different colourings: south is saturated golden yellow-olive with dark blotches, east is a pale sage and cream camouflage mottle, and north is olive-khaki with bold reddish-brown bands. Anatomy and pose agree, but the palette does not.
findings.quote: facings disagree on anatomy/palette, or a structure does not turn with the body
findings.fix: Paint all three facings in one shared variant colouring, the pale sage-and-cream mottled chitin with gold plate rims seen on east, so south and north match east plate for plate.

findings.seen: At 32 px per cell the juvenile is a very small pale fleck, and its pincers and antennae disappear.
findings.quote: does not read at 32 px/cell (advisory by the brief)
findings.fix: Keep the body mass compact with a value contrast against sand that is clear enough for the body to read as one distinct pale shape at 32 px.
